title: Reacting thermals (reactive-convection), SIMDE: burning caps formed from a random hot field rise on their own vortex pair into fresh fuel, travel 3+ body lengths between their own birth and their own fission (11/18, 6/9, 5/14 dividing caps on seeds 0-2), reach generation 5-8, and all go out within 2 t when the fuel is emptied; the g=0 reaction-diffusion twin divides but no dividing spot travels 3 lengths
summary: world.py (the sighting's world, with the fork now emptying the fuel at fork_t) is a 2D Boussinesq fluid in vorticity-streamfunction form with heat T made only by burning a fast-diffusing, regrowing fuel Y (r = A Y T^2/(T^2+Ti^2)[T>Tc], heat loss h, Lewis number 0.05); T=0 is absorbing, so every new body comes from an existing one. labkit packs at 1 t per frame (seeds 0-2, 128^2, T=600): persistent splits 33/21/24, max generation 8/5/7, merge/split 0.12/0.24/0.23; divmove.py (labkit's own segmentation and tracker) finds dividing caps born by a split that travel >= 3 sqrt(area) between their own birth and division in 11/18, 6/9 and 5/14 (2/18, 4/9, 1/14 in long-axis lengths), nearly all upward. dt/2 (world step 0.04 -> 0.02): 29 persistent splits, generation 7, 16/23 pass. Fuel fork at t=400 (Y set to 0, regrowth off): 17 -> 0 and 25 -> 0 bodies by t=402 against 26 and 20 in the fed runs (efork.png). The g=0 twin (same reaction-diffusion, no flow) makes still splitting spots: 8/14 persistent splits, generation 2, 0/5 and 0/6 dividing spots pass 3 lengths.

claims.statement: In each of seeds 0-2 a random hot field on uniform fuel burns out to 1-3 pockets that become crescent caps; each cap rides its own counter-rotating vortex pair upward into fresh fuel, leaves a burnt wake, stretches into an arc and sheds an arm that curls into a new cap. Caps divide persistently to generation 5-8 with few merges, most dividing caps travel 3 or more sqrt(area) between their own birth and their own division, and every cap goes out within 2 t when the fuel is emptied while the fed twin keeps 20-26.
claims.track: seed 0, track 112 (strip_s0_t112.png; pack/seed0/divmove.json): born by a split at t=163, rises 58 px = 9.4 sqrt(area) (4.2 long axes) to its own division at t=277, burning fuel throughout; its lineage is in pack/seed0/lineage.png and it and all its descendants go out at the t=400 fork in pack_fork/seed0

controls_run.E: pack_fork/ (fuel emptied at t=400, seeds 0 and 1) against pack/ (fed twin, same seeds); efork.json
controls_run.M: pack_g0/ (g=0: same reaction-diffusion without flow, seeds 0 and 1): 0/11 dividing spots travel 3 lengths
controls_run.D: pack_dthalf/ (world step halved, seed 0): 29 persistent splits, generation 7

claims.bd_control: g=0 twin (pack_g0, seeds 0 and 1): the same reaction-diffusion with the buoyancy torque off divides (8 and 14 persistent splits, generation 2) but its spots stay put: 0 of 11 dividing spots travel 3 sqrt(area), against 22 of 41 with flow. The twin lost M; it kept D and E.

limits: Motion is buoyant rise: its direction is set by gravity, a uniform field (not a gradient), and the buoyancy exists only because the cap burns, so M is self-generated thrust along a fixed axis; reviewers should decide whether a uniform gravity counts as an imposed field. E is close to construction: heat is made only by burning and decays at h, so emptying the fuel must put every body out; the fork shows the bodies die, not just decline. Bodies are hot spots in a fluid, not material: there is no conserved body matter and no boundary layer (no B claimed). Long-axis body lengths pass far less often than sqrt(area) (7/41 vs 22/41); caps move broadside, which the protocol allows for sqrt(area). 128^2 periodic box only, no resolution test (the world has no dx parameter yet), T=600. The tracker still counts ~150 nucleations per run: sub-threshold warm fragments crossing the T threshold, not spontaneous ignition (T=0 is absorbing).
